title: 2019 Written Reflections
overview: Nerves were high as both teams looked to kick off the highly anticipated first annual Cyder Cup. Just when everyone thought this match would come bursting out of the gates, they did just the opposite, putting in the slowest 9 of the tournament driven by errant drives, scenic views, and ice cold ciders.
writeup: Session 1 | Fourball | August 3, 2019
Tobiano Golf Course
The first annual Cyder Cup kicked off with two fourball matches at the stunning Tobiano Golf Course in Kamloops, BC.
Match 1 - Team Navy (Meakings / Wells) defeats Team Red (Griffiths / Bradley) 2&1

Nerves were high as both teams looked to kick off the highly anticipated first annual Cyder Cup. Just when everyone thought this match would come bursting out of the gates, they did just the opposite, putting in the slowest 9 of the tournament driven by errant drives, scenic views, and ice cold ciders.

With the group behind making their presence known with threatening tee shots all afternoon, pace (and thankfully play) picked up on the back-nine. There was little to seperate the two teams for most of the match until the team of Meakings and Wells both hit the dance floor on the par 3 17th, finishing off with tap in pars and a 2&1 victory.
Match 2 - Team Navy (Bleim / Collister) defeats Team Red (Bromley / Catliff) 7&5

Dominance. The only word to describe this match. Team Navy set the tone for the tournament, winning the first hole and never relinquishing the lead. Team Red played courageously, but were unable to mount a comeback at any point in the match and ulitmately succumbed to the strong play and team chemistry of Bleim and Collister.
Session 2 | Beer Olympics | August 3, 2019

To seperate the men from the boys, teams competed in a best-of-seven drinking games contest at the end of Day 1. Team Red charged in front with wins in the first rounds of beer pong, baseball, and flip cup to take a 3-0 lead. This lead was however short lived, as Team Navy staged a heroic comeback, winning the boat race, highly controversial relay, round of baseball, and then finally the dramatic game 7 beer pong final.
Session 3 | High-low | August 4, 2019
The Dunes Golf Course
After a panicked wake up and a mad dash to make a 9:00am tee time in Kamloops, Day 2 kicked off with a high-low match at The Dunes Golf Course in Kamloops, BC.
Match 1 - Team Navy (Bleim / Wells) defeats Team Red (Bradley / Bromley)

This match saw Dylan Bradley shoot his best round of the tournament, tapping in on the 18th hole for a 95. However, channelling their inner Fleetwood and Molinari, silver club winners Eric Bleim and Steve Wells came away with the victory.
The highlight of this match did not occur on the putting greens, but rather in the golf carts, with Dylan Bradley taking down an impressive 7 beers and a self-imposed Cyder.
Match 2 - Team Red (Catliff / Griffiths) defeats Team Navy (Collister / Meakings)

This match opened with a BANG. After finding the green in regulation on the first hole, Team Red captain Sam Griffiths fell victim to a Cyder at the hands of Team Navy's JJ Meakings. When it seemed that Griffiths would be down for the count before this match had even started, he stepped up to drain the 20 foot birdie putt and give his team an early lead. Stellar play from Kevin Catliff, along with Griffiths's tournament low score of 81, led the team to a wire-to-wire victory, giving Team Red their much needed first point of the tournament.
Session 4 | Singles | August 4, 2019
Sun Peaks Golf Course
The tournament ended as the teams competed in four singles matches to determine the winner of the first annual Cyder Cup at the Sun Peaks Golf Course in Sun Peaks, BC.
Match 1 - Team Navy (Bleim) defeats Team Red (Catliff)

Two fierce competitors faced-off in the lead-off match of the singles session. Coming off two wins in the team matches, Team Navy captain Eric Bleim was, as the kids say, "feeling himself." Kevin Catliff was unphased.

Bleim took a comanding lead in the front-nine thanks to a hot putter. However, with his accurate play off the tee, Catliff staged a comeback on the back-nine and was able to pull the match within 2 going into the 16th hole. The match concluded in spectacular fashion with Catliff draining a par putt on the 16th green from 30 feet away and Bleim responding with a 15 foot birdie putt of his own to win the match 3&2.
Match 2 - Team Navy (Meakings) halves the match with Team Red (Griffiths)

These two heavyweights traded blows all afternoon in what shaped up to be the rivalry of the tournament. After being paired together and each taking a point in the first two sessions, Meakings and Griffiths went to battle in the singles session. With little between them on the front-nine, Griffiths pulled ahead on the back to take a 2 up lead.

With the sun setting and the beers flowing on the 15th hole, the match took a turn in what will stand as one of the golfing highlights from this year's tournament..."IT'S IN THE HOLE!" With none of group paying close enough attention (and his teammate Bleim even mistaking it for his own ball), Meakings holed out from 130 yards, winning the hole with an eagle and cutting the lead to 1. The two went back and forth for the remaining 3 holes, and in the end this match ended the only way it could've, with the two competitors taking half a point and each finishing the tournament 1/1/1. Could this be the beginning of a Cyder Cup rivalry for years to come?
Match 3 - Team Navy (Collister) defeats Team Red (Bradley)

Team Navy's George Collister came to play in the singles session, breaking 90 for the first time and finishing with an outstanding 83 on the Sun Peaks golf course. To continue his struggles in the first two matches, Team Red's Dylan Bradley was unable to respond with any strong play of his own, leading to a 0-3-0 record and a date with "the shoe." Bradley did, however, get his revenge in the evening by murdering Collister in a rap battle.
Match 4 - Team Navy (Wells) defeats Team Red (Bromley)

It may have been something in the water (or the 22 beers he drank throughout the weekend), but Steve Wells proved to be an unstoppable force for Team Navy. This match saw Wells pick up his third win of the tournament and an undefeated record.

While Sean Bromley played with heart, he was unable to overcome the strong play of Wells. Fighting darkness and multiple requests from the marshal to get off the course, Wells and Bromley were barely able to complete the final match of the Cyder Cup.

title: 2020 Written Reflections
overview: It was clear that Team Red had been waiting all year for a chance at redemption, with Bromley and Griffiths taking a 5 up lead on the front-nine. As Meakings proceeded to shank balls off the tee on the back-nine, Wells refused to go down without a fight, making clutch pars to bring the match within two. However, after weathering the dreaded "double cyder" to Griffiths on the par 3 12th, Team Red was able to hang on for the win, taking their first lead (and Bromley's first point!) in tournament history.
writeup: Session 1 | Fourball | August 1, 2020
Tobiano Golf Course
The second annual Cyder Cup kicked off with two fourball matches at Tobiano Golf Course in Kamloops, BC.
Match 1 - Team Red (Bromley / Griffiths) defeats Team Navy (Meakings / Wells) 3&2

It was clear that Team Red had been waiting all year for a chance at redemption, with Bromley and Griffiths taking a 5 up lead on the front-nine. As Meakings proceeded to shank balls off the tee on the back-nine, Wells refused to go down without a fight, making clutch pars to bring the match within two. However, after weathering the dreaded "double cyder" to Griffiths on the par 3 12th, Team Red was able to hang on for the win, taking their first lead (and Bromley's first point!) in tournament history.
Match 2 - Team Red (Bradley / Catliff) defeats Team Navy (Bleim / Collister) 4&3

While Bleim and Collister came in with sky-high confidence after a successful 2019 tournament, their brashness was soon diminished due to the strong play of Bradley in the first 5 holes of the match. Catliff also began his strong play on the tough par 3 7th hole by sticking his tee shot to 25 feet and making an easy par (while both Team Navy players lost their balls in the abyss). With their consistent ball striking, Team Red took an early lead and never looked back.

The only highlight for Team Navy occurred when the foursome thought Collister made a hole-in-one from the blind tee-shot of 15th hole. However, the ball ended up 10 feet from the hole and Collister missed his birdie putt, ending any chance of a Team Navy comeback. Team Red wins 4&3.
Session 2 | Beer Olympics | August 1, 2020
Beer Olympics

In an updated format for this year's tournament, teams competed in three best-of-three series drinking matches at the end of Day 1 with 3 points up for grabs. After losing both matches in the morning session, it was clear that Team Navy was ready to drink as they cruised to a first match beer pong victory 2-0. Team Red however was able to bounce back quickly to win baseball 2-0. In the final match of flip cup, teams traded blows early on, splitting the first two games and pushing to a deciding game 3. As Team Navy got out to a quick start and Meakings headed over to the scorers table to record the victory, Team Red mounted a comeback for the ages with four straight single flips to win the game and take the match 2-1. Rumour has it Collister's cup is yet to be flipped to this day.
Session 3 | High-Low | August 2, 2020
Eaglepoint Golf Resort
Day 2 kicked off with a high-low match at Eaglepoint Golf Resort in Kamloops, BC.
Match 1 - Team Navy (Bleim / Wells) defeats Team Red (Bradley / Catliff) 1 UP

The match got off to a slow start when Wells realized he had "lost" his phone in the middle of the second fairway. After taking 15 minutes to scour the first hole, it was finally determined that Wells' phone had been in Bleim's pocket the whole time. There were few highlights to be had from that point forward. The match was filled with bad golf, lost balls and slow play. Ultimately, Team Navy took the 1UP win after triple-bogies from Catliff and Bradley on the 18th hole - a fitting end for this dreadful match.
Match 2 - Team Navy (Collister / Meakings) defeats Team Red (Bromley / Griffiths) 4&3

With how the flip cup match ended on Day 1, a weaker man wouldn't have gotten a wink of sleep, but Team Navy captain George Collister must've slept like a baby based on his dominant performance in session 3. Along with partner JJ Meakings, the two took the lead early and never looked back, ultimately closing out the match on the par 3 15th with a stellar approach shot from Collister.
Session 4 | Singles | August 2, 2020
Bighorn Golf & Country Club

The tournament went into session 4 at the Bighorn Golf & Country Club in Kamloops, BC with the score at 4-3 in favour of Team Red. With 8 points up for grabs, the tournament all came down to the final 4 matches.
Match 1 - Team Red (Catliff) defeats Team Navy (Bleim) 7&5

The much anticipated rematch between Catliff and Bleim turned out to be a let down. Catliff was at the top of his game - hitting greens, draining putts, and making pars. Bleim, on the other hand, battled to make contact with the golf ball.  While Bleim did his best to blame the beatdown on on the sunscreen in his eyes, it was clear that he was outmatched from the first hole. The largest blowout in Cyder Cup history was cemented with Catliff's win on the 13th green at Big Horn.
Match 2 - Team Red (Griffiths) defeats Team Navy (Meakings) 4&3

Meakings brought everything he had to the session 4 singles match, but this year nothing could stop Team Red from claiming the full point. After a birdie on the par 3 4th and an early 3 up lead, not even a tee box cyder on the 6th could stop Griffiths from cleaning up another birdie and taking a 4 up lead on the front.

Doing his best Happy Gilmour impression, Meakings scrambled for a par on the 12th after shattering the windshield of one of our humble patrons to win the hole, but unfortunately that was the lone highlight (or lowlight?) for Team Navy on the back-nine as steady play from Griffiths maintained the lead and eventually closed out the match on 15.
Match 3 - Team Navy (Wells) defeats Team Red (Bromley) 1 UP
After a match that went the distance in 2019, this matchup between Team Red's Sean Bromley and Team Navy's Steve Wells may well have been the most highly anticipated singles rematch of 2020.

Seeing his teammates struggle around him and knowing that the cup was all but lost, a weaker man may have thrown in the towel, but Wells fought to the very end in an attempt to maintain his stellar Cyder Cup record. Once again, this match came down to the 18th green, and dispite Bromley battling all round long, it was Wells once again who emerged victorious. Will anyone be be able to slow down Wells and his 5/1/0  record?
Match 4 - Team Red (Bradley) defeats Team Navy (Collister) 3&2

The 2019 singles match between these two saw George go lights out through 18 holes as Bradley had no answer to his career-best round. This year though, Bradley was determined to avoid a date with "the shoe" again.

After a nervy start from both players, Bradley took the lead on the front 9. As they were nearing the turn, Collister began to make a charge, making a long par putt on 11. This move was short lived as Bradley immediately answered with a 15' putt of his own to halve the hole. This putt would prove to be the turning point as Bradley was able to cruise to victory securing the win 3&2, ultimately solidifying Team Reds' entry to the winner's circle for 2020.

title: 2021 Written Reflections
overview: The opening match featured four Cyder Cup veterans who knew exactly what to expect from one another. Sam Griffiths' steady leadership kept Team Red within striking distance throughout the front nine, while Sean Bromley did what Sean Bromley does best—grinding out halves and providing a steady stream of chirps from tee to green. Unfortunately for Team Red, Steve Wells quietly went about his business, hitting fairways with robotic consistency and making golf look far easier than it should. Whenever Red looked poised to steal momentum, Eric Bleim answered with a clutch putt, reminding everyone how dangerous he can be when the flatstick heats up. Navy closed the match on the 16th hole, taking the first point of the weekend.
writeup: Session 1 |  Fourball | July 8, 2021
Tobiano Golf Course

The third edition of the Cyder Cup returned to the breathtaking Tobiano Golf Course overlooking Kamloops Lake. After Team Red captured the Cup in 2020, Captain Dylan Bradley looked to defend his title, while Team Navy arrived determined to reclaim the trophy. The opening fourball matches have historically set the tone for the weekend, and this year proved no different—although perhaps not in the way Team Red had hoped.
Match 1 – Team Navy (Wells / Bleim) defeats Team Red (Griffiths / Bromley) 3&2

The opening match featured four Cyder Cup veterans who knew exactly what to expect from one another. Sam Griffiths' steady leadership kept Team Red within striking distance throughout the front nine, while Sean Bromley did what Sean Bromley does best—grinding out halves and providing a steady stream of chirps from tee to green. Unfortunately for Team Red, Steve Wells quietly went about his business, hitting fairways with robotic consistency and making golf look far easier than it should. Whenever Red looked poised to steal momentum, Eric Bleim answered with a clutch putt, reminding everyone how dangerous he can be when the flatstick heats up. Navy closed the match on the 16th hole, taking the first point of the weekend.
Match 2 – Team Navy (Meakings / Collister) defeats Team Red (Catliff / Bradley) 4&3

The second match had plenty of fireworks. Dylan Bradley's aggressive style produced moments of brilliance—including a ripped drive that nearly reached a short par four—but also found enough trouble to keep Team Red on the defensive all afternoon. Kevin Catliff did his best to steady the ship, repeatedly finding fairways and giving his team chances to claw back into the match. Across the fairway, JJ Meakings and George Collister seemed to feed off one another's energy. Collister produced several spectacular recovery shots from places golfers should never visit, while Meakings mixed clutch birdies with the occasional animated conversation with his golf clubs. The result was another convincing Navy victory and an unexpected clean sweep of the opening session.
Session 2 | 2-man Scramble | July 9, 2021
Talking Rock Golf Resort

With Team Navy carrying all the momentum, the scramble matches at Talking Rock became a must-win opportunity for Team Red. The challenging layout punished overly aggressive golf, forcing both teams to rely on teamwork, patience and timely putting rather than heroics.
Morning Scramble – Team Navy defeats Team Red (4 Under)

Team Navy continued their impressive start by piecing together one of their most complete rounds of the weekend. The pairing of Meakings and Collister complemented each other beautifully, with one player seemingly always bailing out the other after the occasional adventurous tee shot. Red generated chances throughout the day but watched several birdie attempts burn the edge, allowing Navy to extend their tournament lead.
Afternoon Scramble – Team Red defeats Team Navy (4 Under)

With the tournament beginning to slip away, Team Red finally found the response they desperately needed. Bromley and Catliff played mistake-free golf while Bleim and Wells appeared to lose their way at the most inopportune time. The confident win by Team Red meant the scramble session was split, preventing Navy from running away with the Cup and ensured Sunday would still have plenty of drama.
Session 3 | Singles |July 10, 2021
Sun Peaks Golf Resort

Entering the singles matches, Team Navy appeared firmly in control. History, however, has repeatedly shown that no lead is safe in the Cyder Cup, and Team Red produced one of the greatest Sunday performances the tournament has ever seen.
Sean Bromley defeats George Collister 2&1

Sean Bromley got Team Red off to the perfect start. Staying true to his reputation as the tournament grinder, Bromley refused to give away holes and slowly wore Collister down with steady golf. George flashed moments of brilliance, including an improbable par save after finding terrain better suited for mountain goats than golfers, but Bromley's consistency proved too much. Team Red had their first point, and suddenly the comeback felt possible.
Dylan Bradley defeats Steven Wells 3&2

Tasked with taking down the quietly dominant Steve Wells, Captain Dylan Bradley embraced the challenge. Bradley's aggressive style paid dividends early as he strung together several birdies to build an advantage, while Wells continued doing everything in his power to make the match uncomfortable. In the end, Bradley refused to let momentum slip away, securing a huge victory that breathed life into Team Red's chances.
Sam Griffiths defeats Eric Bleim 5&4

If there was one performance that defined Sunday, it belonged to Sam Griffiths. Calm, composed and seemingly incapable of missing the middle of the clubface, Griffiths steadily dismantled Bleim over fourteen holes. Every time Bleim looked ready to make a charge, Griffiths answered with another fairway, another green, or another clutch putt. The 5&4 scoreline hardly flattered him, as the Team Red captain produced one of the most complete singles performances in Cyder Cup history.
Kevin Catliff defeats JJ Meakings 1 Up

With the Cup hanging in the balance, Kevin Catliff and JJ Meakings delivered the match of the day. Catliff once again showcased why he has earned a reputation as one of the tournament's most consistent golfers, rarely missing a fairway or putting himself in trouble. Meakings countered with moments of brilliance—including a lengthy birdie putt that drew cheers from both teams—but also displayed the emotional rollercoaster that has become part of his game, complete with one club receiving an unscheduled lesson in aerodynamics. Fittingly, the match remained undecided until the 18th green, where Catliff calmly rolled in a nervy par putt to seal a 1 Up victory and complete Team Red's remarkable clean sweep.
2021 Tournament Reflection

The 2021 Cyder Cup will forever be remembered as the tournament that showcased just how quickly momentum can change. Team Navy stormed out of the gates with a commanding sweep of the opening fourball matches before the teams traded blows during the scramble session. Trailing heading into Sunday, Team Red responded with four outstanding singles victories, completing one of the greatest comebacks in tournament history and capturing the Cup by a 9-6 scoreline. Captain Dylan Bradley successfully defended Team Red's title, while Steve Wells' consistently excellent play and sportsmanship earned him the inaugural People Champ Award. The third edition of the Cyder Cup served as another reminder that no lead is ever safe once Sunday singles begin.

title: 2022 Written Reflections
overview: For the first time in tournament history, the Cyder Cup left Kamloops and made the trip to beautiful Pemberton, British Columbia. With Team Red looking to defend their dramatic 2021 comeback, Captain JJ Meakings had one objective in mind: bring the Cup back to Team Navy. The opening fourball matches provided the perfect opportunity for Team Red to continue their recent momentum.
writeup: Session 1 | Fourball | August 19, 2022
Sunstone Golf Club

For the first time in tournament history, the Cyder Cup left Kamloops and made the trip to beautiful Pemberton, British Columbia. With Team Red looking to defend their dramatic 2021 comeback, Captain JJ Meakings had one objective in mind: bring the Cup back to Team Navy. The opening fourball matches provided the perfect opportunity for Team Red to continue their recent momentum.
Match 1 – Team Red (Griffiths / Bromley) defeats Team Navy (Bleim / Wells) 6&5

The defending champions wasted little time making their intentions known. Sam Griffiths once again proved why he's one of the tournament's steadiest competitors, calmly guiding Team Red around Sunstone Golf Club while allowing Sean Bromley to embrace his usual role as chief chirper. Bromley somehow found time to compliment Navy's good shots while simultaneously reminding them of every missed putt. Across the fairway, Eric Bleim flashed moments of brilliance with a hot putter, but Team Navy struggled to string together enough consecutive holes to build momentum. Team Red steadily pulled away on the back nine to secure the opening point.
Match 2 – Team Navy (Meakings / Collister) defeats Team Red (Bradley / Catliff) 2&1

The second match was every bit as entertaining. Dylan Bradley embodied his "go big or go home" mentality, producing mammoth drives that left both teams wondering whether they should applaud or search the trees. Kevin Catliff quietly cleaned up the mistakes, repeatedly finding fairways and giving Team Red countless birdie opportunities. JJ Meakings battled hard, producing a spectacular birdie from long range that swung the momentum Team Navy’s way, while George Collister delighted everyone with several miraculous recoveries after exploring parts of the golf course not shown on the scorecard. Team Navy ultimately completed the come back, putting Captain Meakings first points on the board for Team Navy.
Session 2 | 2-man Scramble | August 20, 2022
Big Sky Golf Club

All square entering Saturday, Team Navy felt the need to push. Big Sky Golf Club offered wide fairways, breathtaking mountain views, and exactly the type of golf course where momentum could change in a hurry.
Morning Scramble – Team Navy (Wells / Meakings) defeats Team Red (Bradley / Catliff) with a winning score of 3 under par

If Friday morning belonged to Team Red, Saturday morning belonged entirely to Team Navy. The chemistry between Navy's pairings was evident from the opening holes, with each player seemingly taking turns producing the shot the other needed. Long birdie putts began disappearing into the middle of the cup, confidence returned, and the chirping shifted to the opposite side of the fairway. By the final green, Team Navy had secured the points.
Afternoon Scramble – Team Red (Griffiths / Bromley) defeats Team Navy (Bleim / Collister) with a winning score of 2 under par

The afternoon session felt eerily similar. Team Navy generated plenty of opportunities but simply couldn't convert enough of them. Meanwhile, Sam Griffiths quietly continued doing Sam Griffiths things—fairways, greens and two or three putting—while his teammates capitalized whenever an opening presented itself. By day's end, Team Red had remarkably erased Friday's disappointment and entered Sunday's singles with everything to play for.
Session 3 | Singles | August 21, 2022
Nickolas North Golf Club

After two days of outstanding golf, everything came down to singles. With the Cup tied, every hole suddenly carried a little more weight, every conceded putt became a discussion, and every group seemed to attract a growing gallery as the afternoon wore on.
George Collister defeats Dylan Bradley 2UP

George Collister delivered one of his finest Cyder Cup performances. Known as the tournament's wild card, George somehow mixed brilliant approach shots with recoveries from places that defied explanation. Bradley refused to go quietly, grinding over every putt and ensuring nothing came easily, but Collister's timely birdies proved decisive as Team Navy struck first on Sunday.
Steve Wells defeats Sean Bromley 3&2

Few singles matches featured two more contrasting styles. Bromley attacked nearly every flag he could see, while Wells patiently plotted his way around Nickolas North with surgical precision. Time and again, Bradley produced moments that had spectators shaking their heads in amazement before following them with equally adventurous misses. Wells never blinked. His trademark consistency earned another valuable point and reinforced his reputation as one of the Cup's most dependable players.
Sam Griffiths defeats Eric Bleim 4&2

With the two Cyder Cup founders facing off, expectations were high, and neither disappointed. Griffiths once again looked every bit the composed Sunday performer that Team Red has come to rely upon, and Bleim tried to do everything he could to hold on. Several lengthy putts found the bottom of the cup, allowing Griffiths and his Team Red to edge ahead in one of the highest-quality matches of the tournament.
JJ Meakings halves with Kevin Catliff
Every great Cyder Cup deserves a dramatic finish, and 2022 certainly delivered.

Entering the closing stretch, neither player could create any separation. Catliff continued his trademark display of consistency, fairway after fairway keeping constant pressure on his opponent. Meakings responded the only way he knows how—with emotion. One hole featured a towering birdie putt and fist pump, while another saw a golf club briefly reconsider its relationship with gravity after an errant approach. The gallery following the match grew larger with every hole as word spread that the Cup would likely be decided here.

Standing on the 18th tee, the tournament itself remained undecided. Both players found the fairway before exchanging solid approaches, setting up matching par opportunities. Catliff rolled his putt safely home before Meakings calmly matched him moments later. The two shook hands, halving the match and, in doing so, securing the final half point Team Navy needed to reclaim the Cyder Cup by the slimmest of margins.
Sometimes, half a point feels like a full victory.
2022 Tournament Reflection

The fourth edition of the Cyder Cup may go down as the most competitive tournament in the event's history. Team Red looked strong in the Friday's fourball matches, only for Team Navy to answer with a strong performance of their own during Saturday's scramble sessions. With the tournament perfectly poised entering singles, both captains received outstanding performances from their teams before the entire weekend came down to the final match on the course. JJ Meakings' hard-fought halve against Kevin Catliff proved enough to secure an 8-7 Team Navy victory and return the Cup to blue. While the margin was only a single point, the tournament showcased everything the Cyder Cup has become known for: competitive golf, unforgettable moments, relentless chirping, and friendships that somehow survive three straight days of match play. Sam Griffiths was deservedly recognized as the People Champ, while Captain JJ Meakings lifted his first Cyder Cup as captain in one of the most memorable finishes the tournament has ever produced.

title: 2025 Written Reflections
overview: Team Red wasted little time making a statement. Sam Griffiths continued his reputation as one of the tournament's most dependable leaders, calmly steering his side around Fairmont's demanding layout while rarely putting himself out of position. Across the fairway, JJ Meakings showed flashes of brilliance with several towering iron shots and a lengthy birdie conversion that briefly swung momentum, but the consistency of Team Red proved difficult to overcome. The match remained close throughout, though Red's timely putting over the closing holes earned them the opening point of the weekend.
writeup: Session 1 | Fourball | August 12, 2025
Big Sky Golf Club

Six years after the inaugural Cyder Cup, the tournament arrived in Whistler for what many considered the most picturesque edition yet. Captain Eric Bleim returned looking to defend Team Navy's dramatic one-point victory from 2022, while Team Red, led by Sam Griffiths was eager to reclaim the Cup. With the towering Coast Mountains surrounding Big Sky Golf Club, the stage was set for another unforgettable weekend.
Match 1 – Team Red (Griffiths / Bradley) defeats Team Navy (Collister / Meakings) 5&4

Team Red wasted little time making a statement. Sam Griffiths continued his reputation as one of the tournament's most dependable leaders, calmly steering his side around Fairmont's demanding layout while rarely putting himself out of position. Across the fairway, JJ Meakings showed flashes of brilliance with several towering iron shots and a lengthy birdie conversion that briefly swung momentum, but the consistency of Team Red proved difficult to overcome. The match remained close throughout, though Red's timely putting over the closing holes earned them the opening point of the weekend.
Match 2 – Team Navy (Bleim / Wells) defeats Team Red (Catliff / Bromley) 4&3

Any concern that Team Navy might find themselves chasing the tournament disappeared in the afternoon match. Steve Wells once again quietly demonstrated why teammates love having him on their side, hitting what felt like every fairway on the property. George Collister supplied the entertainment, following one miraculous recovery shot with another drive that nearly reached the adjacent fairway. Somehow, it all worked. Team Navy's combination of steady golf and timely heroics proved too much for Team Red, leaving the opening session evenly split and the tournament perfectly poised heading into Day Two.
Session 2 | 4-man Scramble |  August 13, 2025
Fairmont Chateau Golf Club

Saturday introduced one of the biggest format changes in Cyder Cup history: the inaugural Team Vs. Team 4-man Scramble. Rather than traditional head-to-head matches, every player contributed toward a single team score. Team Red was first off the tee, giving them the opportunity to post a target before Team Navy teed off just minutes behind them. Throughout the afternoon, word travelled between groups as birdies were made, putts dropped, and the projected winning score constantly shifted. The format proved to be an instant success, with every player invested in every hole until the final putt was holed.
Team Red produced an excellent score, one that likely would've won on most weekends. The pressure, however, only seemed to motivate Team Navy.

Led by Steve Wells' trademark consistency and several monster tee balls from JJ Meakings, Navy slowly chipped away at Red's total. Every update passed between the groups tightened the atmosphere, and by the closing stretch it had become apparent that the tournament's momentum was hanging in the balance. The lads in blue found a new gear on the back nine, posting an incredible score of 57 (15 under par), allowing Team Navy to edge Team Red in the inaugural All Vs. All Scramble and seize control of the tournament heading into Sunday's singles.

The new format immediately earned rave reviews from both teams, combining the camaraderie of a scramble with the pressure of team match play. More importantly for Captain Meakings, it handed Team Navy a crucial point—and all of the momentum.
Session 3 | Singles | August 14, 2025
Whistler Golf Club

Despite trailing entering singles, Team Red remained confident that history could repeat itself. After all, this was the same team that had completed the famous Sunday sweep just four years earlier. Team Navy, however, had learned from history—and this time had no intention of letting another Cup slip away.
George Collister defeats Dylan Bradley 5&4

George Collister continued what had quietly become the best golf of his Cyder Cup career. Equal parts spectacular and unpredictable, George mixed towering approach shots with miraculous escapes from places spectators were convinced required hiking boots rather than golf shoes. Bradley battled relentlessly, as always, refusing to concede anything easily while delivering enough chirps to keep both groups entertained. In the end, George's birdie on the closing stretch proved decisive and gave Team Navy the perfect start.
Kevin Catliff defeats Steven Wells 3&2

Watching Steve Wells play match play golf had become something of a recurring nightmare for Team Red. Once again, Wells simply refused to make mistakes. Catliff embraced his trademark steady-Eddie approach, producing several incredible shots that drew applause from both teams before following them with equally adventurous recoveries. While Wells’ respectable round provided plenty of entertainment, Catliff quietly accumulated pars and slowly closed the door, earning a much needed point for Team Red.
JJ Meakings defeats Sam Griffiths 1UP

Two of the tournament's fiercest competitors met once again with valuable points on the line. Griffiths lived up to his reputation as the ultimate fairway finder, repeatedly forcing Meakings to earn every hole. JJ responded with exactly the type of performance Team Navy had come to expect in big moments. A curling birdie putt on the back nine ignited an emotional celebration that could probably be heard across Whistler, while a perfectly struck long iron into the closing stretch effectively sealed the match. There may have been one, two, or even three clubs tossed earlier in the afternoon, but by the 18th green, JJ had channeled every bit of that emotion into securing another crucial point for Team Navy.
Eric Bleim defeats Sean Bromley 5&4

Fittingly, the final match featured two of the tournament's dark horse competitors. Neither player was willing to give an inch, trading pars, bogeys and double bogeys throughout the afternoon. Bromley remained as composed as ever, while Bleim once again demonstrated why he becomes so dangerous whenever his putter catches fire. Once the putter got hot, EB never looked back, cruising to a 5&4 win, putting an exclamation point on Team Navy’s defiant victory.
2025 Tournament Reflection

The sixth edition of the Cyder Cup marked another evolution of the tournament. Whistler provided a spectacular backdrop, the introduction of the All Vs. All Scramble proved an overwhelming success, and the quality of golf continued to improve across the board. While Team Red struck first during the opening session, Team Navy responded by winning every remaining team format and carried that momentum into Sunday's singles. Captain JJ Meakings successfully defended the Cup with a convincing 10-5 victory, but perhaps the biggest story belonged to George Collister. Long known as the tournament's lovable wildcard, George paired his trademark personality with consistently outstanding golf throughout the weekend, earning the 2025 People Champ Award in a well-deserved recognition of both his play and the energy he brought to every group. By the time the final putt dropped on the 18th green at Whistler Golf Club, one thing had become abundantly clear: six years in, the Cyder Cup had grown into far more than just a golf trip. It had become an annual tradition, built on competition, friendships, unforgettable moments, and stories that somehow seem to get even better every time they're told.
